h: Choice Foreknowledge and Repentance from Love

p: בְּתַנְחוּמָא (וַיֵּשֶׁב ג) פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ
— In Tanchuma (Vayeshev 3) on this parashah
עַל פָּסוּק: "וְיוֹסֵף הוּרַד מִצְרָיְמָה" (בְּרֵאשִׁית לט, א),
— on the verse: “And Joseph was brought down to Egypt” (Genesis 39:1),
פָּתַח בְּדִין הַבְדָּלָה עַל נֵר שֶׁל עוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת,
— it opened with the halakhah of Havdalah over the candle of idolaters,
וּמַיְיתֵי מַעֲשֶׂה בְּאַנְטוֹנִינוֹס וְכוּלֵי
— and cites the incident involving Antoninus, etc.,
שֶׁאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא:
— wherein Rabbi Chiya said:
זְבוּבִין אֵלּוּ וְאוֹתוֹ לִגְיוֹן שָׁוִין וְכוּלֵי;
— these flies and that legion of soldiers are equal, etc.;
אָמַר לוֹ: כָּל כָּךְ נָתַן רַבִּי חִיָּיא הַבַּבְלִי מַמָּשׁ הִשְׁוָה אוֹתָן וְכוּלֵי,
— Antoninus said to him: to such an extent did Rabbi Chiya the Babylonian ascribe significance to equate them, etc.,
אֲבָל זְבוּבִין הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עוֹשֶׂה שְׁלִיחוּתוֹ בָּהֶן וְכוּלֵי,
— yet through flies the Holy One, blessed be He, executes His divine mission, etc.,
וְכֵן "וְשָׁלַחְתִּי אֶת הַצִּרְעָה" (שְׁמוֹת כג, כח),
— and likewise “And I will send the hornet” (Exodus 23:28),
וּבְכִנִּים וּצְפַרְדְּעִים וְכוּלֵי.
— and through lice and frogs, etc.

p: וְיֵשׁ לְהָבִין,
— And this needs to be understood:
הָא מִקְרָא מְפוֹרָשׁ הוּא:
— behold it is an explicit scriptural verse:
"הוֹי אַשּׁוּר שֵׁבֶט אַפִּי וּמַטֶּה הוּא בְיָדָם זַעְמִי" (יְשַׁעְיָה י, ה),
— “Woe Asshur, the rod of Mine anger, in whose hand as a staff is Mine indignation,”
וַהֲרֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עוֹשֶׂה שְׁלִיחוּתוֹ עַל יָדָם!
— and thus the Holy One, blessed be He, certainly executes His mission through them!
וְהַנְּבִיאִים נִתְנַבְּאוּ עַל אַשּׁוּר וּנְבוּכַדְנֶאצַּר שֶׁעֲתִידִין לַעֲשׂוֹת,
— And the prophets explicitly prophesied concerning Assyria and Nebuchadnezzar what they were destined to perpetrate,
וּמַה מַעֲלִיּוּתֵיהּ דִּזְבוּבִין וְכַדּוֹמֶה
— so what is the unique spiritual virtue of flies and their like
שֶׁאָמַר שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עוֹשֶׂה שְׁלִיחוּתוֹ עַל יְדֵיהֶם?
— that he asserted that the Holy One specifically executes His mission through them alone?

p: אַךְ הָעִנְיָן הוּא עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁכָּתַב הָרַמְבַּ״ם (פֶּרֶק ו מֵהִלְכוֹת תְּשׁוּבָה הֲלָכָה ה)
— However, the underlying matter is based on what Maimonides wrote (Hilkhot Teshuvah 6:5)
שֶׁאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁגָּזַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא: "וַעֲבָדוּם וְעִנּוּ אֹתָם" (בְּרֵאשִׁית טו, יג),
— that even though the Holy One, blessed be He, decreed: “and they shall serve them, and they shall afflict them”,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם לֹא נִפְטְרוּ הַמִּצְרִיִּים,
— nevertheless the Egyptians were not exempted from punishment,
מֵאַחַר שֶׁלֹּא גָּזַר עַל אִישׁ יָדוּעַ,
— since He did not decree against any specific named individual,
אֶלָּא הוֹדִיעוֹ שֶׁסּוֹף זַרְעוֹ עָתִיד לְהִשְׁתַּעְבֵּד וְכוּלֵי,
— rather merely informed Abraham that eventually his offspring were destined to be subjugated, etc.,
וְכָל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד מֵאוֹתָן הַמִּצְרִיִּים וְהַמְּרֵיעִים לְיִשְׂרָאֵל,
— and every single one of those Egyptians who mistreated Israel,
אִלּוּ לֹא רָצָה לְהָרַע לָהֶם – הָרְשׁוּת בְּיָדוֹ, עַיֵּין שָׁם.
— had he not wished to harm them, the free choice was in his hand, see there.
וְהָרַאֲבַ״ד הִשִּׂיגוֹ:
— And the Ra'avad challenged him:
כֵּיוָן שֶׁאֶחָד מוּכְרָח, וְעַל מִי יָחוּל הַגְּזֵירָה? עַיֵּין שָׁם.
— since someone was bound to fulfill it, upon whom then was the decree to fall? See there.

p: אַךְ הַפֵּירוּשׁ נִרְאֶה,
— However, the true explanation appears to be
שֶׁהָעוֹנֶשׁ עַל רְצוֹנָם וַהֲנָאָתָם שֶׁהָיָה לָהֶם בִּשְׁעַת מַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁהֵצֵרוּ לְיִשְׂרָאֵל;
— that retribution was inflicted for their willful desire and sadistic pleasure during the act when afflicting Israel;
וְאִלּוּ הָיוּ עוֹשִׂים רַק לְקַיֵּים הַגְּזֵירָה הַקְּדוּמָה מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
— whereas had they acted solely to execute the primordial decree of Hashem, blessed be He,
הָיוּ עוֹשִׂים כִּזְבוּב הָעוֹשֶׂה בִּשְׁלִיחוּת הַבּוֹרֵא וְאֵין לוֹ שׁוּם הֲנָאָה כְּלָל.
— they would have functioned like a fly that acts on the Creator’s mission having no personal gratification at all.
וְהַצְּפַרְדְּעִים בְּמִצְרַיִם נִכְנְסוּ לָאֵשׁ לְקַיֵּים גְּזֵירַת הַבּוֹרֵא יִתְבָּרַךְ שְׁמוֹ
— And the frogs in Egypt threw themselves into the fiery ovens to fulfill the decree of the Creator, blessed be His Name
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב פְּסָחִים נג:).
— (as written in Pesachim 53b).
וְעַל מַה שֶּׁנֶּהֱנוּ בִּשְׁעַת מַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁהֵצֵרוּ לְיִשְׂרָאֵל בָּא הָעוֹנֶשׁ,
— And specifically for their self-gratification during the act of oppressing Israel did retribution descend,
שֶׁמִּזֶּה מְבוֹאָר שֶׁלֹּא עָשׂוּ מִפְּנֵי הֶכְרֵחַ הַגְּזֵירָה,
— from which it is evident that they did not act out of the pure compulsion of the decree,
שֶׁהֲרֵי לֹא נִגְזַר שֶׁיַּעֲשׂוּ בְּחֵשֶׁק וּבְרָצוֹן.
— for it was never decreed that they execute it with malice, lust, and personal delight.

paragraphs.text: Pesachim 53b: “They drew an a fortiori inference on their own from the plague of frogs in Egypt. With regard to frogs, which are not commanded concerning the sanctification of the name of God, it is written: ‘And the river shall swarm with frogs, which shall go up and come into your house, and into your bedchamber, and onto your bed, and into the houses of your servants, and upon your people, and into their ovens and kneading bowls’ (Exodus 7:28). When are kneading bowls found near the oven? You must say that it is when the oven is hot. If in fulfilling the command to harass the Egyptians, the frogs entered burning ovens, all the more so, we, who are commanded concerning the sanctification of the name of God, should deliver ourselves to be killed in the fiery furnace for that purpose. Apparently, Theodosius taught Torah in public, which indicates that he was a great man.”

p: וְזֶה הַמְכֻוָּון גַּם כֵּן
— And this is likewise the exact meaning
שֶׁבִּזְבוּבִים וְכַדּוֹמֶה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עוֹשֶׂה בָּהֶן שְׁלִיחוּתוֹ,
— that through flies and similar creatures the Holy One, blessed be He, performs His true mission,
כֵּיוָן שֶׁאֵין עוֹשִׂים עַל יְדֵי בְּחִירָתָם וּרְצוֹנָם;
— since they act devoid of human free choice and self-serving will;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן אַשּׁוּר וּנְבוּכַדְנֶאצַּר וְכַדּוֹמֶה,
— whereas with Assyria and Nebuchadnezzar and their like,
אַף שֶׁהֵם כְּלֵי זַעְמוֹ שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא,
— even though they serve as instruments of indignation for the Holy One, blessed be He,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם לֹא שַׁיָּיךְ לוֹמַר שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עוֹשֶׂה בָּהֶן שְׁלִיחוּתוֹ,
— nevertheless it is inappropriate to say that the Holy One executes His pure mission through them,
כֵּיוָן שֶׁעוֹשִׂים בִּרְצוֹן עַצְמָם וְחֶשְׁקָם מַה שֶּׁלֹּא נִגְזַר עֲלֵיהֶם.
— since they act out of their own personal will and appetite which was never mandated upon them.
וְאִם הָיָה מִי מֵהֶם עוֹשֶׂה בְּלֹא רָצוֹן וּבְחִירָה,
— And had any one of them acted without personal will and selfish choice,
רַק כְּמוֹ שְׁאָר בַּעֲלֵי חַיִּים שֶׁעוֹשֶׂה לְהַשְׁלִים הַגְּזֵירָה שֶׁגָּזְרָה יְדִיעָתוֹ הַקְּדוּמָה,
— merely like other animals acting to consummate the decree preordained by His foreknowledge,
לֹא הָיָה נֶעֱנָשׁ כְּלָל.
— he would not have been punished at all.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Ramban, Bereishis 15:14: “Even though I decreed that your offspring would be strangers in a land not theirs, and that they would enslave and afflict them, I will nevertheless judge the nation that enslaves them for what they do to them, and they will not be acquitted on the grounds that they carried out My decree. … When a decree goes out from the mouth of a prophet, one who hears it and wishes to fulfill the will of his Creator as decreed bears no sin; on the contrary, it is reckoned to him as a merit, as was said of Yehu: ‘Because you have done well in carrying out what is right in My eyes… your sons of the fourth generation shall sit on the throne of Israel.’ But if he heard the command and killed out of his own hatred, or to take the victim’s wealth, he is liable to punishment, for his intention was to sin. So Scripture says of Sennacherib: ‘Woe, Assyria, rod of My anger… against an ungodly nation I send him’; and it continues: ‘But he does not intend so, nor does his heart think so; for it is in his heart to destroy.’ That is why he was punished in the end.”

p: וְכֵן יֵשׁ לוֹמַר עִנְיַן מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר:
— And similarly we can explain the verse:
"וְקָם הָעָם הַזֶּה וְזָנָה וְגוֹמֵר, וְחָרָה אַפִּי בוֹ וְגוֹמֵר" (דְּבָרִים לא, טז-יז),
— “and this people will rise up, and go astray, etc., then My anger shall be kindled against them, etc.,”
וּבַגְּמָרָא (סַנְהֶדְרִין צ:) דָּיְיקוּ מִקְרָא זֶה
— and in the Gemara (Sanhedrin 90b) they deduced from this verse
שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא יוֹדֵעַ מַה שֶּׁעָתִיד לִהְיוֹת,
— that the Holy One, blessed be He, knows in advance all that is destined to occur,
וְעַל זֶה שָׁאֲלוּ:
— and upon this they challenged:
אִם כֵּן, לָמָּה יַגִּיעַ לָהֶם הָעוֹנֶשׁ וַחֲרוֹן אַף?
— if so, why should retribution and burning wrath befall them?
אָמְנָם בֶּאֱמֶת, הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בָּרָא הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע שֶׁיְּפַתֶּה אֶת הָאָדָם,
— However in truth, Hashem, blessed be He, created the evil inclination to seduce man,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (קִדּוּשִׁין ל:):
— as they said (Kiddushin 30b):
"בָּרָאתִי יֵצֶר הָרָע",
— “I created the evil inclination”,
אֲבָל הָאָדָם צָרִיךְ לְהִתְגַּבֵּר עָלָיו.
— yet man is duty-bound to overpower it.
וְיֵשׁ לִפְעָמִים שֶׁהָאָדָם אָנוּס
— And there are times when a person is utterly overpowered and coerced
וְלֹא יוּכַל לְהִתְגַּבֵּר עַל הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע,
— and cannot overpower the evil inclination,
כְּמוֹ בְּאָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן בַּמֵּאָה וּשְׁלוֹשִׁים שָׁנָה
— such as occurred with Adam the First during the 130 years
דַּחֲזָא לְאוֹנְסֵיהּ כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (עֵירוּבִין יח:);
— when he experienced involuntary emissions, as they taught (Eruvin 18b);
וַהֲלֹא חָסִיד גָּדוֹל הָיָה וְשָׁב בִּתְשׁוּבָה,
— and behold, he was a great saint and returned in repentance,
וּבְוַדַּאי הָיָה נִזְהָר מֵהִרְהוּר עֲבֵירָה גַּם כֵּן,
— and certainly he guarded himself against sinful thoughts as well,
אֶלָּא עַל כָּרְחֲךָ שֶׁגַּם הַהִרְהוּר הָיָה לְאוֹנְסוֹ
— perforce even the passing sinful thoughts occurred involuntarily
שֶׁלֹּא יָכוֹל לְהִתְגַּבֵּר עַל הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע.
— because he was unable to overpower the ferocious evil inclination.
וְאִם הָיָה כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר וּכְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא,
— And had he attained the stature of Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Akiva,
בְּוַדַּאי גַּם מִזֶּה הָיָה נִיצּוֹל,
— he would certainly have been rescued even from this,
וַ"ה' לֹא יַעַזְבֶנּוּ בְיָדוֹ" (תְּהִלִּים לז, לג),
— and “Hashem will not leave him in his hand” (Psalms 37:33),
וְהָיוּ מַכְרִיזִין עָלָיו בָּרָקִיעַ:
— and they would have proclaimed concerning him in the heavens:
"הִזָּהֲרוּ בִּפְלוֹנִי וּבְתוֹרָתוֹ",
— “Be heedful of so-and-so and his Torah”,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁהִכְרִיזוּ עַל רַבִּי מֵאִיר וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא (קִדּוּשִׁין פא.).
— just as they proclaimed over Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Akiva (Kiddushin 81a).
אַךְ מִפְּנֵי הַקִּלְקוּל מֵהַנָּחָשׁ
— However, on account of the spiritual damage caused by the serpent,
לֹא נֶעֱזַר מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לְהִשָּׁמֵר מִכֹּחַ הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע,
— he was not divinely aided from Hashem to be totally guarded against the inclination,
וְהוֹלִיד וְכוּלֵי.
— and generated spirits, etc.

p: וְכֵן הָעִנְיָן בְּמַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וְקָם הָעָם וְזָנָה",
— And such is the dynamic in the verse: “and this people will rise up, and go astray”:
שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ יוֹדֵעַ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה מִי שֶׁלֹּא יוּכַל לְהִתְגַּבֵּר עַל הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע,
— that Hashem knows there will be individuals unable to overcome the evil inclination,
שֶׁהֲרֵי בָּרָא אוֹתוֹ בְּכֹחַ זֶה;
— since He fashioned the yetzer with this ferocious potency;
וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וְקָם הָעָם הַזֶּה וְזָנָה וְגוֹמֵר",
— and this is why it is written: “and this people will rise up, and go astray, etc.,”
שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לְאוֹנְסוֹ שֶׁלֹּא יוּכַל לְהִתְגַּבֵּר עַל הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע וּלְכוֹבְשׁוֹ.
— meaning it occurs out of coercion wherein he cannot overpower and conquer the evil inclination.
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם נִכְתַּב אַחַר כָּךְ עוֹנֶשׁ עַל זֶה: "וְחָרָה אַפִּי וְגוֹמֵר",
— Nevertheless, subsequent retribution is recorded: “then My anger shall be kindled, etc.,”
שֶׁצָּפוּי לְפָנָיו שֶׁיִּהְיֶה מִי שֶׁיַּעֲשֶׂה בְּחֵשֶׁק וַהֲנָאָה,
— because it is foreseen before Him that there will be those who indulge with lust and voluntary pleasure,
וְלֹא יִהְיֶה כִּזְבוּב וּצְפַרְדֵּעַ שֶׁעוֹשֶׂה רַק לְקַיֵּים גְּזֵירַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וְעוֹשֶׂה בִּשְׁלִיחוּתוֹ.
— and will not behave like a fly or frog that acts solely to execute Hashem’s decree on His mission.
וְאִם הָיָה אָדָם עוֹשֶׂה בְּלֹא שׁוּם הֲנָאָה וְחֵשֶׁק,
— And had a human being acted entirely devoid of pleasure and lust,
רַק כְּמוֹ בַּעַל חַיִּים שֶׁעוֹשֶׂה בִּשְׁלִיחוּת הַבּוֹרֵא יִתְבָּרַךְ,
— merely like an animal acting on the mission of the Creator, blessed be He,
וְכֵן הָיָה עוֹשֶׂה רַק מֵהָאוֹנֶס שֶׁכֵּן גָּזְרָה יְדִיעָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ,
— and had done so solely out of the duress preordained by His foreknowledge,
לֹא הָיָה נֶעֱנָשׁ כְּלָל.
— he would never have been punished at all.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Tzidkat HaTzadik §43: “Sometimes a person faces a trial so great that it is impossible for him not to sin, as the Sages said, ‘What is the son to do?’ In this he is considered completely coerced, and the Merciful One exempts him. Coercion also applies when the inclination’s incitement is so overpowering that it cannot be conquered. If the blessed God turned his heart, this sin is not a sin at all; rather, this was God’s will. Consider what is said in Ketubot about a woman whose experience began under coercion: even if she later cries out that, had he left her, she would have hired him, she remains permitted to her husband. Why? The inclination took hold of her. This is considered complete coercion: although she now wills it, a person cannot subdue an inclination so powerful. There is no punishment, despite the forbidden act, because the act was coerced. But a person himself cannot testify to this about himself, for perhaps he still had the power to subdue the inclination—as I heard concerning Zimri, who erred in this.”

paragraphs.text: Connection: This passage supplies an essential limit to the present account of divine foreknowledge and duress. God may know that an act was wholly coerced, but the person experiencing temptation cannot presume that judgment. He must continue to resist; retrospective divine clarification is not permission to sin.

p: וְאַף שֶׁגַּם חֵשֶׁק זֶה וְהָרָצוֹן נוֹדָע לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
— And even though this lust and will are also known to Hashem in advance,
כְּבָר שָׁב לִשְׁאֵלַת יְדִיעָה וּבְחִירָה.
— this circles back to the classic paradox of Foreknowledge versus Free Choice.
וּכְבָר אָמַרְנוּ שֶׁמַּה שֶּׁכָּתַב הָרַמְבַּ״ם (שָׁם פֶּרֶק ה הֲלָכָה ה)
— And we have already established that what Maimonides wrote (ibid. 5:5)
שֶׁהוּא מַה שֶּׁאָמַר הַנָּבִיא: "כִּי לֹא מַחְשְׁבוֹתַי מַחְשְׁבוֹתֵיכֶם וְגוֹמֵר" (יְשַׁעְיָה נה, ח),
— aligning with the prophet’s declaration: “For My thoughts are not your thoughts, etc.”,
נִתְכַּוֵּון גַּם כֵּן לְמַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר חָדָשׁ,
— intended likewise that which is written in the Zohar Chadash:
שֶׁבִּמְקוֹם שֶׁיֵּשׁ יְדִיעָה אֵין בְּחִירָה כְּלָל,
— that in the realm where absolute Foreknowledge reigns there is no free choice at all,
וְיֵשׁ מָקוֹם שֶׁבָּרָא הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁנִּמְסַר הַבְּחִירָה לָאָדָם.
— and there is a realm that Hashem created wherein free choice is truly entrusted to man.

paragraphs.text: Zohar Chadash, additional passage on Vayera 1–2: “‘Everything is foreseen’ in thought, for the Holy One knows his evil thought, while freedom is given to man in action… Rabbi Yosei said: After He showed him each generation and its leaders, surely it became known whether they were righteous, wicked, or intermediate? He answered: It is certainly so; but the secret of the matter is deep: ‘The hidden things belong to Hashem our God.’” The passage distinguishes divine foreknowledge in thought from the freedom given to a person in action, while acknowledging the depth of their relationship. Rav Tzadok develops this into his explanation of the realm of foreknowledge and the created realm of human choice.

p: וּלְעָתִיד יְבָרֵר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
— And in the ultimate future Hashem, blessed be He, will clarify
עַל יְדֵי שֶׁיַּעֲשׂוּ כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל תְּשׁוּבָה מֵאַהֲבָה,
— through all Israel performing repentance out of love,
שֶׁיִּהְיוּ זְדוֹנוֹת נַעֲשׂוֹת כִּזְכִיּוֹת.
— that willful transgressions are transformed into merits.
וְהוּא מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (שַׁבָּת פט:):
— And this is what they taught in Shabbat (89b):
"אִם יִהְיוּ חֲטָאֵיכֶם כַּשָּׁנִים" (יְשַׁעְיָה א, יח) –
— “Though your sins be as scarlet (shanim)” –
כַּשָּׁנִים הַלָּלוּ שֶׁסְּדוּרוֹת וּבָאוֹת מִשֵּׁשֶׁת יְמֵי בְרֵאשִׁית וְעַד עַכְשָׁיו.
— like these solar years that are preordained and orderly from the six days of Creation until now.
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁבְּמַאֲמַר "בְּרֵאשִׁית" נִזְכַּר "תֹּהוּ וָבֹהוּ",
— And this signifies that in the primal creation utterance was mentioned “unformed and void”,
שֶׁמְּרַמֵּז עַל מַעֲשֵׂיהֶן שֶׁל רְשָׁעִים, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ב, ה),
— which alludes to the deeds of the wicked, as written in Bereishit Rabbah (2:5),
וְהוּא שֶׁבֶּאֱמֶת גָּזְרָה כֵּן חָכְמָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ שְׁמוֹ כְּשֶׁהֶאֱצִיל הַבְּרִיאָה:
— for in absolute truth His divine wisdom decreed when emanating the cosmos:
שֶׁיִּהְיֶה "בְּרֵישָׁא חֲשׁוֹכָא וַהֲדַר נְהוֹרָא",
— that there be “first darkness and then light”,
דְּלֵית נְהוֹרָא אֶלָּא הַהוּא דְּנָפֵיק מִגּוֹ חֲשׁוֹכָא, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב, קפד עַמּוּד א),
— for there is no true light except that which emerges from within darkness (Zohar II 184a),
וְאָז "כַּשֶּׁלֶג יַלְבִּינוּ" – שֶׁזְּדוֹנוֹת נַעֲשׂוֹת כִּזְכִיּוֹת.
— and then “they shall be as white as snow”—willful sins transformed into merits.
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁאָז יְבָרֵר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה הַדָּבָר נַעֲשֶׂה בִּבְחִירָתוֹ כְּלָל,
— Meaning that Hashem will then unveil that the matter was not enacted through free choice at all,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב הָאֲרִ״י זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה
— and as the holy Ari of blessed memory wrote
שֶׁבִּמְקוֹם שֶׁיֵּשׁ יְדִיעָה אֵין בְּחִירָה כְּלָל.
— that wherever Foreknowledge rules there is no choice whatsoever.
וְהוּא, שֶׁבְּשֶׁבַע מִדּוֹת תַּחְתּוֹנִיּוֹת, שֶׁהֵם שִׁבְעַת יְמֵי בְרֵאשִׁית, שָׁם הַבְּחִירָה נְתוּנָה;
— Namely: within the seven lower attributes, the seven days of Creation, choice is operative;
וּבְשָׁלֹשׁ רִאשׁוֹנוֹת, בְּעַתִּיקָא, אֵין בְּחִירָה בֶּאֱמֶת,
— whereas within the three supernal attributes, in Atika, choice does not exist in truth,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁיְּבוֹרַר אַחַר שֶׁיִּזְכּוּ עַל יְדֵי תְּשׁוּבָה מֵאַהֲבָה שֶׁזְּדוֹנוֹת נַעֲשׂוֹת כִּזְכִיּוֹת.
— and as will be clarified when they merit through teshuvah from love that sins become merits.

p: וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בַּפָּרָשָׁה: "דִּרְשׁוּ ה' בְּהִמָּצְאוֹ קְרָאֻהוּ בִּהְיוֹתוֹ קָרוֹב, יַעֲזֹב רָשָׁע דַּרְכּוֹ וְגוֹמֵר" (יְשַׁעְיָה נה, ו-ז),
— And this is what Scripture states: “Seek Hashem while He may be found, call upon Him while He is near; let the wicked forsake his way, etc.” (Isaiah 55:6-7),
שֶׁהַמְכֻוָּון שֶׁזּוֹהִי הַתְּפִלָּה שֶׁיִּתְפַּלֵּל לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ: שֶׁיַּעֲזֹב רָשָׁע דַּרְכּוֹ וְכוּלֵי,
— meaning that this itself is the prayer one offers to Hashem: that the wicked forsake his way, etc.,
שֶׁגַּם כֹּחַ הַתְּשׁוּבָה הוּא בְּיַד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
— for even the potency of repentance is in the hand of Hashem, blessed be He,
וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: "קְרָאֻהוּ וְגוֹמֵר".
— and regarding this it is said: “call upon Him, etc.”
וְיוּכַל חַס וְשָׁלוֹם לָבֹא מִזֶּה לִידֵי טָעוּת
— And a person could Heaven forbid fall into error from this
וְלוֹמַר שֶׁאֵין בְּחִירָה כְּלָל, שֶׁהַכֹּל בְּיַד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ;
— and claim that there is no free choice at all, everything being in Hashem's hands;
וּבֶאֱמֶת שֶׁהַיְדִיעָה וְהַבְּחִירָה שְׁנֵיהֶם אֱמֶת וְכָאָמוּר,
— while in truth Foreknowledge and Choice are both absolute truths as stated,
אַךְ שֶׁאֵין כֹּחַ לָנוּ, שֶׁאֲנַחְנוּ בְּעוֹלַם הָעֲשִׂיָּה, לְהָבִין זֹאת,
— only that we in the physical World of Action lack the capacity to comprehend this,
וְעַל זֶה אָמַר הַכָּתוּב: "כִּי לֹא מַחְשְׁבוֹתַי מַחְשְׁבוֹתֵיכֶם וְגוֹמֵר".
— and regarding this Scripture proclaimed: “For My thoughts are not your thoughts, etc.”

p: וְכֵן בְּסוֹף פָּרָשַׁת "שׁוּבָה" כְּתִיב: "מִמֶּנִּי פֶּרְיְךָ נִמְצָא" (הוֹשֵׁעַ יד, ט),
— And so at the end of the section of Shuvah it is written: “From Me is your fruit found” (Hosea 14:9),
וְהוּא גַּם כֵּן מְרַמֵּז עַל הַבֵּירוּר אַחַר שֶׁיַּעֲשֶׂה הָאָדָם תְּשׁוּבָה מֵאַהֲבָה
— which likewise alludes to the ultimate clarification after man repents out of love
שֶׁיִּהְיוּ נַעֲשׂוֹת הַכֹּל כִּזְכִיּוֹת.
— that all sins are transformed into merits.
וּ"פְרִי" נִקְרָא מַעֲשֵׂה הָאָדָם,
— And “fruit” designates the deeds of man,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁמָּצִינוּ לְטוֹבָה (סוֹטָה מו. סוֹף עַמּוּד א):
— as we find applied positively in Sotah (46a):
"שֶׁלֹּא הִנִּיחוּ לַעֲשׂוֹת פֵּירוֹת, מַאי פֵּירוֹת וְכוּלֵי? אֶלָּא מִצְוֹת", עַיֵּין שָׁם;
— “that they did not permit him to bear fruit; what are fruits? Mitzvot”, see there;
וְכֵן (בְּמִדְרַשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת נֹחַ ב):
— and so too in Midrash Tanchuma (Noach 2):
"פְּרִי צַדִּיק וְכוּלֵי – תּוֹלְדוֹתָיו שֶׁל אָדָם אֵלּוּ מַעֲשָׂיו הַטּוֹבִים".
— “The fruit of the righteous, etc.—a person's true offspring are his good deeds.”
וְכֵן בְּהֵיפֶךְ חַס וְשָׁלוֹם נִקְרְאוּ פֵּירוֹת רָעִים,
— And conversely, Heaven forbid, negative actions are called bad fruits,
כְּעִנְיַן מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וַיְקַו לַעֲשׂוֹת עֲנָבִים וַיַּעַשׂ בְּאֻשִׁים" (יְשַׁעְיָה ה, ב).
— in the sense of the verse: “and he looked that it should bring forth grapes, and it brought forth wild grapes” (Isaiah 5:2).
וְאַחַר שֶׁיַּעֲשֶׂה הָאָדָם תְּשׁוּבָה מֵאַהֲבָה,
— And following a person’s repentance out of love,
אָז יְבָרֵר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ: "מִמֶּנִּי פֶּרְיְךָ נִמְצָא",
— Hashem will clarify: “From Me is your fruit found”,
שֶׁכָּל הַפְּעוּלוֹת מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
— revealing that all actions ultimately stem from Hashem, blessed be He,
כְּעֵין מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "כִּי גַם כָּל מַעֲשֵׂינוּ פָּעַלְתָּ לָּנוּ" (שָׁם כו, יב),
— mirroring the verse: “for You also have wrought all our works for us” (ibid. 26:12),
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ: שֶׁסְּדוּרוֹת וּבָאוֹת מִשֵּׁשֶׁת יְמֵי בְרֵאשִׁית.
— and as taught: they were arranged and established from the six days of Creation.

paragraphs.text: Sotah 46a: “Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Shaul says: For what reason did the Torah say to bring a heifer whose neck is broken to a stream? The Holy One, Blessed be He, said: Let something that did not produce fruit, i.e., a heifer that has not given birth, come and have its neck be broken at a stream that flows forcefully, which is a place that does not produce fruit, and atone for the murder of one who was not given an opportunity to produce fruit. The Gemara asks: What is this fruit that he was not given an opportunity to produce? If we say it refers to being fruitful and multiplying, i.e., that the killer prevented him from having more children, but if that is so, in the case of an elderly person or a eunuch, so too will you say that we do not break the heifer’s neck because they could not have had any more children even had they lived? Rather, the fruit are mitzvot, as the killer deprived the victim of the opportunity to perform additional mitzvot.”

paragraphs.text: Midrash Tanchuma, Noach 2: “These are the generations of Noah (Gen. 6:9). R. Tanhuma the son of Abba began the discussion of this subject with the verse: The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life; and he that is wise winneth souls (Prov. 11:30). R. Judah the Levite said: Whenever a man dies childless, he grieves and weeps. Thereupon the Holy One, blessed be He, consoles him with the words: ‘Wherefore do you weep over having left no fruit in this world? You have left fruit that is more desirable than children.’ ‘Sovereign of the universe,’ the man asks, ‘what fruit did I produce?’ The Holy One, blessed be He, replies: ‘The Torah (you observed), concerning which it is written: the fruit of the righteous is a tree of life.’ The verse does not say that children are a tree of life but that the fruit of the righteous is a tree of life. p: רַק אֵיךְ יוּכַל לְהָבִין זֹאת?
— Only how can mortal man grasp this?
עַל זֶה אָמַר הַכָּתוּב:
— Regarding this Scripture proclaims:
"מִי חָכָם וְיָבֵן אֵלֶּה, נָבוֹן וְיֵדָעֵם" (הוֹשֵׁעַ יד, י) –
— “Who is wise, that he may understand these things? Prudent, that he may know them?” (Hosea 14:10) –
הִזְכִּיר שָׁלֹשׁ מִדּוֹת חָכְמָה, בִּינָה, דַּעַת:
— Scripture invokes the three intellectual faculties of Chokhmah, Binah, Da'at:
"חָכָם", "נָבוֹן", "וְיֵדָעֵם".
— “wise” (Chokhmah), “prudent/understanding” (Binah), “and will know them” (Da'at).
וְהוּא שֶׁמֵּחִבּוּר חָכְמָה וּבִינָה יָבֹא הַדַּעַת,
— And this is because from the union of Chokhmah and Binah emerges Da'at,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ בְּמַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "כִּי תָבוֹא חָכְמָה בְלִבֶּךָ וְדַעַת לְנַפְשְׁךָ יִנְעָם" (מִשְׁלֵי ב, י):
— as we noted on: “When wisdom enters into your heart, and knowledge is pleasant unto your soul” (Proverbs 2:10):
חָכְמָה – מוֹחָא, בִּינָה – לִבָּא;
— Chokhmah resides in the brain, Binah in the heart;
וּכְשֶׁיִּתְחַבֵּר חָכְמַת הַמּוֹחַ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה כְּפִי בִּינַת הַלֵּב
— and when brain-wisdom unifies to harmonize with heart-understanding,
יִזְכֶּה לִבְחִינַת הַדַּעַת,
— he merits the attainment of Da'at,
וְיָדוּעַ כִּי הַדַּעַת פְּנִימִיּוּת הַכֶּתֶר,
— and it is known that Da'at is the inner dimension of Keter,
וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר "וְיֵדָעֵם".
— and this is the meaning of “and will know them”.
"כִּי יְשָׁרִים דַּרְכֵי ה'" (הוֹשֵׁעַ שָׁם) –
— “For the ways of Hashem are right” (Hosea ibid.) –
עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וְלֹא דַרְכֵיכֶם דְּרָכָי" (יְשַׁעְיָה נה, ח).
— in the spirit of the verse: “neither are your ways My ways” (Isaiah 55:8).
"וְצַדִּקִים יֵלְכוּ בָם" (הוֹשֵׁעַ שָׁם) –
— “and the just shall walk in them” (Hosea ibid.) –
הַיְינוּ שֶׁהַצַּדִּיקִים מְבָרְרִין אֶת עַצְמָם בְּכָל כֹּחָם בְּמִדַּת הַפַּחַד וְהַיִּרְאָה
— meaning that the righteous clarify themselves with all their might through fear and reverence
לְהִתְגַּבֵּר עַל הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע,
— to overpower the evil inclination,
שֶׁהָרְשׁוּת נְתוּנָה בְּעוֹלַם הָעֲשִׂיָּה;
— since free will is operative in the World of Action;
וְאַחַר כָּךְ, אִם חַס וְשָׁלוֹם יִפְּלוּ בְּיַד הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע,
— and afterward, if they stumble into the grasp of the evil inclination Heaven forbid,
מְבָרְרִין אֶת עַצְמָם עַל יְדֵי תְּשׁוּבָה עִילָּאָה מֵאַהֲבָה.
— they purify themselves through supernal repentance born of love.
וְאָז הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מְבָרֵר אוֹתָם וְאוֹמֵר: "מִמֶּנִּי פֶּרְיְךָ נִמְצָא",
— And then Hashem clarifies them, saying: “From Me is your fruit found”,
וַחֲטָאֵיכֶם כַּשָּׁנִים הַלָּלוּ שֶׁסְּדוּרוֹת וּבָאוֹת מִשֵּׁשֶׁת יְמֵי בְרֵאשִׁית כָּאָמוּר.
— and your sins are like those years pre-set from the six days of Creation, as stated.
"וּפֹשְׁעִים יִכָּשְׁלוּ בָם" (הוֹשֵׁעַ שָׁם) –
— “but transgressors shall fall therein” (Hosea ibid.) –
שֶׁעַל יְדֵי כֵּן יוּכְלוּ הַפּוֹשְׁעִים לְהִתְפַּקֵּר
— for through this dynamic, transgressors may abandon restraint
וְלוֹמַר "דְּלֵית דִּין" חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, כֵּיוָן שֶׁהַכֹּל בָּא מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
— and assert “there is no judgment” Heaven forbid, arguing that all emanates from Hashem.
אֲבָל בֶּאֱמֶת "יְשָׁרִים דַּרְכֵי ה'",
— Yet in truth “the ways of Hashem are upright”,
שֶׁהַכֹּל צָפוּי וְהָרְשׁוּת נְתוּנָה (אָבוֹת פֶּרֶק ג, טו), וְכָאָמוּר.
— for all is foreseen, yet free choice is granted (Avot 3:15), as stated.
